newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends weaker at 482.50/483.50/dlr.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends weaker at 482.50/483.50/dlr.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed slightly softer at 482.50/483.50 with traders attributing the stronger dollar to a lack of currency supply by the Central Bank.
The exchange rate closed at 482.00/483.00 bolivars per dollar Monday.
"There was moderate demand (for foreign currency) in the market, but the Central Bank came in with only a little and that caused the rise (in the rate)," one trader said.
"(The Central Bank) has been using this strategy for a few days and appears to be employing a crawling peg, with mini daily depreciations," he added.
"The Central Bank's supply is small for the size of demand," another trader said.
Traders said recent criticisms by local industrialists that the bolivar was currently 10 percent overvalued had led some clients to buy foreign currency in case of a devaluation.
They said the gradual bolivar depreciation would likely continue Wednesday despite an expected rise in interest rates at the Central Bank's weekly Monetary Stabilization, or TEM, bill auction.
Venezuela continues to pursue an inflation-fighting strong bolivar policy, where the currency ostensibly floats between slowly depreciating bands set by Central Bank intervention.
Critics say the policy has left the bolivar increasingly over-valued with the exchange rate little-changed since price and currency controls were removed in April last year.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
